cards.name: Auto Adjust
cards.summary: One-click tonal and colour correction with no dialog settings: CorelDRAW finds the lightest and darkest values in each colour channel and stretches every channel to the full range, which raises contrast and can also neutralise a colour cast. The result depends entirely on the image: a dull, flat photo gets punchier, while an image that already holds pure black and pure white changes very little.
use_for: quick first-pass fix of a flat, washed-out or slightly tinted product or event photo before layout
batch clean-up of many imported snapshots where per-image tuning is not worth the time
a neutral starting point before a creative grade (Tone Curve, Color Balance) on top
avoid: images that already contain pure black and white (a white caption, a black frame, a colour bar strip like the test plate): the stretch has nothing to stretch and the photo barely changes - use Levels or Tone Curve and set the points yourself
photos whose colour cast is intended (sunset, tungsten mood): the per-channel stretch can remove it - use Levels on RGB Channels together, or Gamma, which move all channels alike and keep the cast
any job that must be reproducible to an exact value: there are no settings to record - use Levels with explicit input/output points

cards.name: Black & White
cards.summary: Converts the image to a greyscale look while letting you decide how light each original colour range becomes: the Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues and Magentas values (range -200 to 300, defaults 40/60/40/60/20/80, the same as Photoshop's Black & White) brighten or darken the grey that each hue turns into. An optional Split tone tints shadows and highlights with two separate hues for a toned print look. The image-slider keys SlideReds ... SlideMagentas default to 0.48/0.52/0.48/0.52/0.44/0.56, which is each colour default rescaled from -200..300 to 0..1 (40 -> 0.48), so they look like the same values on a 0-1 slider scale (inferred from the numbers, not documented).
use_for: black-and-white editorial or poster photo where a red flag, dress or sky must keep separation instead of turning muddy grey
monochrome brand imagery with a controlled tonal mix (darker skies, lighter skin)
split-toned duotone look (cool shadows, warm highlights) for covers and mood boards
avoid: a quick grey with no control: Desaturate is one click
pushing one colour slider far (beyond about +200 or below -100) on a compressed or soft photo: neighbouring areas band and edges halo
a true 1-bit black-and-white bitmap (line art for a stamp, screen print or fax): Black & White keeps smooth greys in the bitmap's colour mode - use Bitmaps > Mode > Black and White (1-bit)

cards.name: Brightness/Contrast/Intensity
cards.summary: The classic three-slider tonal adjustment: Brightness shifts every pixel lighter or darker, Contrast widens or narrows the gap between light and dark, and Intensity strengthens or weakens the lighter tones (its exact maths is not in the harvest). In CorelDRAW 2024 it is still defined in the Effects bar (DrawUI.xml) but the live Effects > Adjust menu no longer shows it, so it is reachable only by its command GUID or effect id.
use_for: opening legacy CorelDRAW documents or macros that used Brightness/Contrast/Intensity
a fast, coarse lift of a dark or flat photo from a script
avoid: new work in CorelDRAW 2024: the item is hidden from the menu - use Effects > Adjust > Light, Levels or Tone Curve, which give finer and better-documented control
large Brightness values: shifting all tones clips highlights (or shadows) to flat white (or black) - use Gamma or Levels' middle value to lift midtones instead
high Contrast on skin or soft video frames: it blocks up shadows and blows highlights

params.does: moves all tones lighter (+) or darker (-)

params.name: Contrast
params.does: spreads (+) or compresses (-) the difference between light and dark

params.name: Intensity
params.does: strengthens or weakens the light tones; exact behaviour not documented

cards.name: Channel Mixer
cards.summary: Rebuilds one output colour channel as a percentage mix of the input channels (RGB, CMYK or Lab), plus a Constant offset. Mixing blue into the red channel, for example, swaps colours (reds go dark, blue turns magenta, warm beige goes green); switching Output to Monochrome makes a custom-weighted black-and-white conversion.
use_for: false-colour and infrared-style looks for posters and album art
channel-weighted black-and-white (Monochrome) with more control than Desaturate
fixing a single contaminated channel (e.g. a scan with a weak blue channel)
avoid: subtle colour casts: Color Balance or White Balance is quicker and more predictable
keeping overall brightness: when the source percentages of a channel add up to more than 100% (see the total readout) the channel brightens and clips - keep the total near 100%
CMYK print images unless you understand channel maths: small mixes cause large ink shifts

cards.name: Color Balance
cards.summary: Shifts the colour of the image along three opposing axes - Cyan to Red, Magenta to Green, Yellow to Blue - either for the whole image (Master) or separately for shadows, midtones and highlights, optionally keeping luminance so brightness does not change. The harvested Mode list has only three entries (3-Way Color, Master, Shadows), so the exact set of views in the dialog is not fully recorded.
use_for: warming or cooling a photo to match a brand palette or a layout's mood
cinematic split grade: teal shadows with warm highlights
removing a colour cast from indoor or fluorescent-lit photos
avoid: heavy shifts with Preserve luminance off: brightness changes along with colour and the image can look muddy
neutralising a cast from a known grey point: White Balance (temperature/tint) is faster
changing one specific hue (only the red flag): use Hue/Saturation/Lightness with a colour channel or Selective Color

cards.name: Desaturate
cards.summary: Removes all colour in one click, turning every pixel into its grey equivalent while the bitmap keeps its RGB/CMYK colour mode, so colour can be added back on top later. No settings: reds, greens and blues of similar brightness end up as similar greys.
use_for: fast greyscale photo behind coloured type or a colour overlay
muted background images so a foreground product or headline pops
a neutral base before tinting with Color Balance or a lens
avoid: photos where differently coloured areas of similar brightness must stay distinct (a red flag on a green field): they merge into one grey - use Black & White or Channel Mixer (Monochrome) to weight each colour
converting for a greyscale-only print workflow: the file stays in colour mode - use Bitmaps > Mode > Grayscale (8-bit)

cards.name: Equalize
cards.summary: Histogram equalization: redistributes the image's tones so they spread across the whole range, which pulls detail out of flat, foggy or underexposed images and usually gives a hard, high-contrast result. Model chooses the target distribution (Uniform or Hyperbolic); the meaning of Channel, Preserve Color and the Lower/Upper limits is inferred from their names (likely the channel to equalize, equalizing brightness without shifting hues, and the part of the histogram that is used), because the harvest could not read their defaults or ranges.
use_for: rescuing detail from a hazy, low-contrast scan or video frame
a gritty, high-contrast documentary or poster look
revealing hidden detail in dark areas before a more careful grade
avoid: portraits and skin: equalization exaggerates noise and blotches - use Levels or Tone Curve
images with large flat areas (sky, studio backdrop): they band and posterize
scripts that need exact values: the defaults and the ranges of LowerLimit/UpperLimit are unknown - leave them and Channel out of the command and set only Model and Preserve Color

cards.name: Gamma
cards.summary: Applies a gamma curve to the midtones while pure black and pure white stay put, so it brings out detail in dark or low-contrast areas without clipping highlights. Gamma Value (key Level, 0.1-10, logarithmic slider) is neutral at its default 1.0; in CorelDRAW values above 1 lighten the midtones and values below 1 darken them (direction stated from experience, not from the harvest). LevelCompact (-1..1, default 0) has exactly the range of log10 of Level (log10 0.1 = -1, log10 10 = 1, log10 1 = 0), so it is most likely the same value on a compact log slider (inferred from the numbers, not documented).
use_for: lifting murky shadows and midtones in an underexposed photo without blowing out white type or highlights
matching the overall lightness of photos placed side by side in a layout
compensating a print that comes out too dark (dot gain) by lifting midtones
avoid: fixing true black or white points (a grey-looking 'black'): gamma never moves the ends - use Levels
extreme values (below 0.3 or above 4) on compressed images: shadows band and look milky
setting both Level and LevelCompact in one command: LevelCompact appears to be log10 of Level, so two values can conflict - set Level only

params.name: Gamma Value
params.does: the gamma applied to midtones; 1.0 = no change
params.typical: 1.2-1.6 to lift a dark photo, 0.6-0.8 to deepen a washed-out one

pairs_with: Levels (set black and white points first)

large Lightness values: they flatten contrast toward white or black - use Levels or Gamma

cards.name: Levels
cards.summary: The precise tonal-range tool (effect id EqualizeEffect, menu command OnEqualize; not the Equalize item, which is HistogramEqualizeEffect): set the input black and white points to clip and stretch the histogram, a Gamma value for midtones, and output points to compress the range, for all RGB channels together or one channel at a time; Auto Adjust sets the points automatically. Moving InputLow up and InputHigh down gives a crisper, higher-contrast image; raising OutputLow fades blacks to a matte look.
use_for: setting clean black and white points on a flat scan or video frame before print
matte / faded-blacks look for lifestyle and editorial images (raise Output low)
fixing a cast channel by channel (Red, Green, Blue)
the standard tonal correction step in any photo-prep workflow

pulling InputLow / InputHigh far into the histogram: shadows and highlights clip to flat black/white and lose detail
creative curve shapes (S-curves, cross-process): use Tone Curve
